steps.text: Combine chocolate and heavy cream in a nonstick saucepan over medium heat. Stir until chocolate is melted and mixture is smooth.
Mix in hot water, coffee powder, vanilla, and sugar. Continue to heat, stirring frequently, until fondue is smooth.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Fondue
raw_recipe.description: This rich chocolate fondue recipe is easy to make with melted chocolate, cream, and vanilla for a decadently smooth chocolate treat, perfect for dipping!
raw_recipe.name: Chocolate Fondue

review.reviewBody: This is a great fondue with 1/3 freshly brewed coffee or cappuchino instead of the instant powder and water. A tip for the leftovers (because everyone else was right, this does make a lot!)... This recipie is essentialy a truffle recipie. Let the leftovers cool and then refrigerate. Round out small balls and roll in cocoa powder, powdered sugar or toadsted coconut. All of a sudden you have a new, gormet desert you can serve all over again and impress the crowds! Truffles also make great gifts when wrapped nicely!

Delicious and Easy! I did omit the coffee and the water. I used 2 bags of Nestle Milk Chocolate Chips vs the grated chocolate. Made in my fondue pot....Everybody at our gathering loved it...especially on marshmallows, fruit, and rice krispy treats. I had a bit left over and it reheated fabulously in the fondue pot today. Thank you for a great recipe! Happy New Year!

Excellent! Adjusted the recipe to fit my 16 oz mini crockpot little dipper. Melted the ingredients in a sauce pan first then tranfered >>> 2 cups (11.5 oz) ghirardelli milk chocolate chips, 1/2 cup heavy cream, 1 tablespoon water (optional), no instant coffee (due to having kids around). Since the party ended up being an all day thing, I had to plug and unplug the crockpot a couple of times just enough for the chocolate to be warm and not too hot to burn the kiddies. If a cord is not available, just use a bowl and just reheat in microwave. I had used pretzels, strawberries, cubed rice krispies. We also had a little bit left for the next day use; slighty reheat and drizzle over sliced bananas (all we had) for breakfast. It's also great drizzled over vanilla ice cream.

As a fondue, I'd have to say that I wasn't overly impressed - which is why I rated it a 3. It was good, but nothing spectacular. However, I noted that many other reviewers made truffles with the leftovers and I have to say, that as a truffle center - this was absolutely AMAZING! I rolled them into 1-inch balls, froze them for an hour or so then made a coating (16 oz chocolate chips & 3 tbls shortening, melted) to dip them in. Everyone LOVED them - even a co-worker who isn't really into sweets raved about them.

I prefer less sweet chocolate than milk chocolate so I used Ghirardelli semi-sweet chocolate to give it a darker more intense flavor. Didn't have any instant coffee on hand so I omitted that and the 1/3 c of hot water. I added 2 oz of Grand Marnier in its place. This gave it a wonderfully subtle hint of orange to the richer chocolate flavor. Will definitely make another time

I used a combination of a ratio of 2/3 milk chocolate chips to 1/3 semi-sweet chocolate chips. I used Ghiradelli brand chocolate chips. I used the suggestion to cut back on the water a bit and I dissolved the coffee ahead of time and heated up the cream a bit before adding the chocolate. Was a big hit!

This was ahhhmazing!!! I couldn't decide between this one or the Flaming Turtle recipe from The Melting Pot so I mixed the recipes together. I did this one first, except I probably doubled the coffee granuals and skipped the water and sugar, just heated a bit of the cream in the microwave and disolved the coffee in there. Then I added about a 1/2 a cup of caramel ice cream topping and a cup of toasted pecans. In fairness to this recipe, I tasted it before I tweaked and it was perfect. I just wanted caramel and pecans!! We were fishing and fighting for the pecans and the caramel gives a great texture that coats dippers well. I'd serve this to guests either way in a heartbeat, I loved the coffee kick! Thanks! :)

I made a half batch of this recipe and eliminated the water. I used half a bag of dark chocolate chips and 1/2 bag of semi sweet chips. Kids and adults enjoyed it and the chocolate coated various fruits, marshmallows and pretzels nicely. Great flavor! I put the excess in a glass dish and topped it with nuts and heath brittle and put it in the fridge. Once it cooled it was like a cross between a chocolate bar and fudge and every bit as delicious.

Served this at my Christmas party this year. I did this right in my fondue pot on low. Substituted 1/4 c fresh espresso for the instant coffee and water. I wanted a less sweet, more "adult" taste, so used dark chocolate instead of milk chocolate. It was a huge hit with cubes of pound cake, bananas, strawberries and sugar cookies!

Easy & delicious! I deviated and cut this recipe in half since we were serving 8. I used half dark chocolate (60% cacao) and 1/2 milk chocolate. I used coffee instead of water and omitted the instant coffee. I also omitted the sugar. The best dippers seemed to be mini pretzels! Other dippers included under ripe bananas, strawberries, marshmallows, biscotti and graham crackers. I will edit then I try the suggestion to use the leftovers to make truffles :)
Amazing! Used a dash of Bailey's instead of coffee and didn't add the water. Consistency and flavor were already perfect! I used 2 bags Ghiradelli chocolate and one Nestles.

Substituted espresso for the water and used 1/2 semi sweet 1/2 milk. Ended up being a bit too dark for me so next time I'll use more milk chocolate. Also, just know the recipe makes A LOT. I had 8 people over and was left with a massive amount of leftover chocolate. I'd suggest halving the recipe unless you're feeding a massive group.

This is a good recipe but, as others stated, it does make a lot. It melted quickly right in my fondue pot. I did 2 parts milk chocolate/1 part semi sweet. We had oreos, pound cake, marshmallows, strawberries and twist pretzels for dipping.

Cut the recipe in half for 3 people and it still was a lot. Used 1/2 dark chocolate and 1/2 German chocolate. Next time I will stick to just milk chocolate or mostly milk chocolate as I found the dark chocolate was too rich (and I usually prefer dark chocolate). Very easy and good recipe for fondue.
this fondue is so rich and delicious! i loved the coffee taste!

Made this recipe this weekend. I used 1/3 cup of espresso instead of the coffee and water. I also substituted 2/3 of the chocolate for semi-sweet chocolate instead of milk chocolate. Served with marshmallows, pound cake, raspberries and strawberries. Next time I'd like to try bacon and donut holes as dippers as well.

Made this recipe this weekend. I used 1/3 cup of espresso instead of the coffee and water. I also substituted 2/3 of the chocolate for semi-sweet chocolate instead of milk chocolate. Served with marshmallows, pound cake, raspberries and strawberries. Next time I'd like to try bacon and donut holes as dippers as well.
So good! Used coffee instead of water.

I make this every year for Valentines Day. My family loves it! I serve with all the fruit other people listed, but also crushed nuts (the banana in the fondue dipped in the nuts is amazing, as is the marshmallow). But don't forget to have some potato chips on hand! The salty sweet is soooo good!
